Toyota Recalls 19,000 Electric C-HR Crossovers, Battery Overcharge Condition To Blame
7 photos
Photo: Toyota
The world's largest automaker is recalling an estimated 19,000 examples of the C-HR+ worldwide. Known as C-HR in North America due to the lack of an internal combustion alternative in said part of the world, the full-electric sport utility vehicle may experience an overcharge condition during regenerative braking due to a software fault in the EV control unit.
According to Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt, namely the German Federal Ministry for Transport, vehicles produced between June 17, 2025, and July 9, 2026, feature the subject EV control unit software. Said unit manages the electric drive system of the zero-emission crossover, which is produced at the Takaoka plant for all markets. Takaoka is also the home of the mechanically related Subaru Uncharted.
Toyota explains that EV-ECU software can allow a nearly full high-voltage battery to overcharge during regeneration operation, making this a battery management issue. Regeneration operation, meanwhile, is when energy is recovered by lifting off the accelerator or pressing the brake pedal. Regenerative operation, therefore, feeds energy back into the high-voltage battery.
Lithium-ion batteries for EV applications have a limited charge window, and if the EV-ECU software doesn't manage the flow of energy correctly, the battery can exceed its safe operating range. When this happens, overcharging triggers a bunch of warning messages and shuts down the electric drive system. The loss of motive power at high speeds understandably increases the risk of a crash.
The German market accounts for 1,096 of the affected vehicle population, and the KBA further highlights that said campaign is under investigation. Authorized Toyota dealers will gladly reflash the subject control unit free of charge, yet the Japanese automaker has not published a whole lot of relevant details for European models, including when the remedy software will become available.
Photo: Toyota Thankfully, we do know this problem has two North American counterparts in the US and Canadian markets. The US recall covers 8,521 units of the C-HR, with production dates ranging between February 6, 2026, and July 10, 2026. Its filing describes the very same fault and remedy, with Toyota Motor North America further mentioning that said problem was discovered as part of internal testing.
So far, the company reported zero warranty claims and field reports potentially related to the described condition. Over in Canada, recall number 2026421 covers 1,311 units of the 2026 model year C-HR electric sport utility vehicle. Said campaign was issued on September 2, 2026, and replaces an earlier safety recall.
As noted earlier, C-HR+ is what its maker calls the model in the Old Continent, making it easy to distinguish from the internal-combustion alternative. By internal combustion, yours truly is referring to either a hybrid or a plug-in hybrid. These models pack either 1.8- or 2.0-liter naturally aspirated I4s. The C-HR+ is underpinned by a different platform, specifically the e-TNGA rather than TNGA-C.
Advertised with 150-kW DC fast-charging capability, the C-HR+ for Europe offers two battery and three powertrain options. Base means 57.7 kWh and 123 kilowatts going to the front wheels alone, whereas the mid-range version ups the ante to 77 kilowatt-hours and 165 kilowatts. The top configuration adds an 88-kW rear motor, resulting in 343 ps (338 hp) and 438 Nm (323 lb-ft) of torque.
Available from nearly 35,000 euros in Germany, the C-HR+ is listed with anything from 458 to 607 kilometers (285 to 377 miles) in the WLTP on a full charge. Its battery pack, be it the smaller or larger unit, comes with a 10-year warranty.

1,400-HP Twin-Turbo C8 Corvette Z06 Runs 9.0 Quarter-Mile, Grenades From Too Much Extra Torque
31 photos
Photo: YouTube/Late Model Racecraft
When the C8 Corvette Z06 entered the chat, the world said, “Oh, that’s cute,” and moved on with business as usual. Then the ZR1 blew the doors off competitors, and things got pretty interesting. Twin-turbo steroids suddenly made the “cute” sportscar a hypersonic missile. Chevrolet wasn’t done yet, and the hybrid ZR1X proved that in full. But the ZR1 opened a pandora box of inspiration.
Did Chevrolet really expect American gearheads to politely wait in line and sell a kidney for the 1,064-horsepower C8 Corvette ZR1 without strapping two colossal hairdryers onto the more domestic Z06 in their own garages first? Naturally, the moment Bowling Green proved that twin-turbocharged forced induction belonged on a mid-engine flat-plane-crank V8, Houston-based tuning specialist Steven Fereday and his team at the Late Model Racecraft YouTube channel answered the call.
In its standard factory configuration, the 2024 Chevrolet Corvette Z06 is an engineering marvel powered by the naturally aspirated 5.5-liter LT6 V8. Featuring dual overhead camshafts, titanium intake valves, sodium-filled exhaust valves, three throttle bodies, and a 12.5:1 compression ratio, the stock engine screams to 8,600 rpm while delivering 670 horsepower at 8,400 rpm and 460 lb-ft of torque at 6,300 rpm (680 PS, 624 Nm), putting down 550 to 580 rear-wheel horsepower (558-588 PS).
Paired with an 8-speed dual-clutch transaxle, the showroom-stock coupe rockets from 0 to 60 mph in 2.6 seconds, clears the standing quarter-mile in 10.6 seconds at 131 mph (211 kph), and reaches a top speed of 195 mph (314 kph). However, Steven Fereday waited until HP Tuners unlocked full Engine Control Module and Transmission Control Module calibration before collaborating with Extreme Turbo Systems to transform his personal Z06 into a forced-induction development test mule.
Photo: YouTube/Late Model Racecraft The custom rear-mounted setup pairs low-slung Precision ball-bearing turbochargers with factory exhaust headers, TIG-welded stainless-steel piping, dummy center exhaust tips, and a dedicated dual-scavenging oil pump system that prevents oil from pooling inside the low-hanging housings. Cooled by an air-to-water intercooler with its own heat exchanger and fan, the untouched LT6 engine retains its factory camshafts and idles like stock while cured of its low-rpm torque deficit under positive boost.
In initial street testing on 6 to 7 psi of wastegate pressure, the package generated 800 to 850 rear-wheel horsepower on 93-octane pump gas and over 900 rear-wheel horsepower on higher-octane fuel.
After upgrading the fuel system for E85 ethanol and adding a boost controller, dyno testing yielded a staggering 1,285 rear-wheel horsepower (1,303 PS) at 8,558 rpm and 812 lb-ft of rear-wheel torque (1,101 Nm) at 7,014 rpm. That’s around 1,430 flywheel horsepower and 893 lb-ft, with a 10% driveline loss (1,450 hp, 1,211 Nm).
Photo: YouTube/Late Model Racecraft Because the local Baytown drag strip near Houston closed years ago, Fereday and his crew hauled the gray Corvette four-and-a-half hours north to the Texas Motorplex in Ennis for its quarter-mile debut. Expecting a conservative 9.2-9.4-second opening run on a soft launch tune, Fereday was stunned when the car effortlessly clocked 9.061 seconds at 158.48 mph (255 kph) on its very first pass with a gentle 1.478-second 60-foot split time.
So composed was the chassis at speed that Fereday joked the run felt like a leisurely 10-second pass, even as onboard Dragy telemetry recorded 4.14 seconds from 60 to 130 mph (97-209 kph) and 3.98 seconds from 100 to 150 mph (161-241 kph). For the second run, the team added intercooler ice and extra boost, netting a 9.013-second pass at 157.70 mph (254 kph) with a 1.458-second 60-foot time despite minor factory clutch slippage down track.
Determined to break into the 8-second zone on the third attempt, Fereday skipped the intercooler ice, increased dual-clutch transmission clamping pressure, sharpened the third-to-fourth gear shift, and raised the launch boost. That extra greed proved instantly fatal to the drivetrain: right at the hit of the throttle, the Z06 violently sheared a hollow factory inner axle stub clean in two before it could even leave the prepped starting line surface.
Photo: YouTube/Late Model Racecraft Although the car already wore upgraded Drive Shaft Shop CV axles, its stock inner stubs could not survive more than double the factory horsepower . After spending two hours installing a replacement factory stub sourced 30 minutes away from Roshan at Boost District, Fereday staged at dusk for a fourth pass with a softer launch, only to snap the second axle stub just like that on the very same starting line.
Refusing to surrender, Fereday stayed a second day after GForce Performance Engineering overnighted solid billet inner stubs and matching heavy-duty CV axles to the track. Yet on the fifth attempt, the Corvette revved without moving an inch; the new billet hardware held firm, revealing that the first stub failure had fatally damaged the rear differential assembly inside, which also explained why the second stock stub had sheared so very effortlessly.
These growing pains highlight why an aftermarket twin-turbo Z06 and a factory C8 ZR1 are not mechanical twins, even though both use 5.5-liter flat-plane-crank V8 engines. While the Z06's LT6 and ZR1's 1,064-horsepower LT7 share a 104.25 mm bore and 80 mm stroke, the LT7 drops compression from 12.5:1 to 9.8:1 via dished forged pistons, larger 60 cc chambers, stronger rods, and a rebalanced crankshaft with an 8,000 rpm redline.
Photo: YouTube/Late Model Racecraft Furthermore, whereas the LT6 relies solely on eight direct fuel injectors, the LT7 adds secondary port injection for sixteen total injectors supporting up to 24 psi of boost. Unique cylinder head castings, forced-induction camshaft profiles, manifold-integrated Mar-M alloy turbochargers, head-mounted intercoolers, and a factory-reinforced transaxle distinguish Chevrolet's fiery flagship.
So, the short answer is No, one can’t simply bolt on a pair of turbos on a stock Z06 and go around bullying proper ZR1s without expecting some instant karma kicks in the groin. However, Late Model Racecraft have a point: with strengthened driveline internals, a boosted Z06 is already knocking on the 8-second drag strip door. Then again, adding heavy-duty parts to the Z06 is getting intimately close to home-brewing a ZR1 recipe. Which one’s your cup of tea?

VW Teases New Hot Hatch, Concept Appears To Be Based on the ID. Polo GTI
7 photos
Photo: Instagram | volkswagen
Volkswagen recently took to its social media channels to drop a couple of teaser images of a brand new concept car, which is part of the brand’s 50-year celebration since the original Golf GTI came out.
Therefore, while the VW Group may indeed axe roughly half of its entire lineup by 2035, the GTI emblem is here to stay. And it is used not only on the compact hot hatch, namely the Golf, but also on the latest Polo. And as you already know, the supermini has gone down the battery-electric route for the new generation.
Christened the Volkswagen ID. Polo , it celebrated its debut more than half a year ago, with production commencing a couple of months later, in June 2026, at the Martorell factory in Barcelona, Spain. It was previewed by the ID.2all Concept in 2023, and is based on the VW Group’s MEB Entry platform. Therefore, it shares its nuts and bolts not only with its high-riding sibling, the ID. Cross, but also the Skoda Epiq and Cupra Raval.
The zero-emission supermini is 159.6 inches (4,053 mm) long, 71.5 inches (1,816 mm) wide, and 60.2 inches (1,530 mm) tall. The footprint is similar to that of its predecessor, and at 102 inches (2,600 mm) long, the wheelbase is a bit longer. Since it’s an EV, it is also heavier, as it has a curb weight of almost 1.6 metric tons or nearly 3,500 pounds. By comparison, the Mk6 Polo weighed from 1.1 to almost 1.4 metric tons (about 2,400-3,000 lbs), depending on the spec.
Photo: Instagram | volkswagen Now, as far as the teased model goes, it sits under a cover, and had its pictures taken from two angles. One of the images shows its front fascia with the headlights on from beneath the cover, and the other shows it from the side. And it looks like the concept is actually based on the ID. Polo GTI . The new Volkswagen study is a couple of days away from being unveiling, as the debut is scheduled for this Friday (November 20, 2026), the Instagram post embedded at the bottom of the story reveals.
So, what exactly is new? Well, from what we can tell, it seems that the front bumper is part of the novelties, and we wouldn’t be surprised to learn that the air intake in the middle has been significantly enlarged compared to the regular Volkswagen ID. Polo GTI. Chances are that fender flares could be part of the makeover, alongside perhaps other things on the sides, and the back end also features something new.
As you can clearly see from one of the teasers, this study has a massive rear wing at the back, which makes it look like it belongs at the racetrack rather than on public roads. It is possible that the rear bumper and diffuser could also be new, and so could the wheels, for that matter. We’d also expect some changes on the inside, where the concept in question could look a lot more aggressive than the Volkswagen ID. Polo GTI .
We have yet to see the cockpit of the new concept car, but chances are it might be stripped down, featuring a pair of bucket seats for the driver and front passenger, a deleted rear bench, a roll cage for safety purposes, some carbon fiber trim, and a few other changes. However, this is our two cents, and should be taken accordingly for obvious reasons.
Photo: Volkswagen Some believe that the study might actually serve as a preview for the Volkswagen ID. Polo GTI Clubsport, though we will believe it when we see it. Nevertheless, that does not mean that we do not want to see such a thing, because it will make the electric supermini hot hatch a lot more interesting, not to mention faster, and more aggressive.
Between us, we wouldn’t be surprised if Volkswagen decided to keep the powertrain details of the upcoming concept car a secret, but since it is based on the ID. Polo GTI, it should get the same assembly. What does this mean? Well, 223 horsepower (166 kW/226 ps) produced by its front-mounted electric motor, which drives the front wheels, because all versions of the ID. Polo are FWD in case you forgot.
The GTI sits at the very top of the new Volkswagen ID. Polo family. In its homeland of Germany, it starts from 39,995 euros (equal to $43,995), offering a 431-km (268 miles) range on the WLTP cycle with the 52 kWh battery pack fully charged.
Lesser models include the Style and Life, priced from 32,395 euros ($35,635) and 27,995 euros ($30,795), respectively, and the most basic version of the car comes from 24,995 ($27,495), and is called the Trend. Instead of a 52 kWh battery pack, which is also found on the mid-range models, the entry-level has a 37 kWh unit, and a WLTP -rated range of 334 km (208 miles). Acquiring a biotech with an existing Big Pharma partner can impose financial and strategic constraints around data sharing and milestone and royalty payments—but it is “rarely a deal-breaker,” according to one biotech consultant.
When a large pharma company acquires a smaller developer, the purchase may come with baggage. Beyond the company’s assets—just the platform technology, pipeline of candidates, perhaps a small portfolio of commercial products, plus a skilled workforce—the buyer may also get a thorny co-parenting arrangement with a rival powerhouse.
But that’s what Merck KGaA could get early next year if the German pharma finalizes its $1.1 billion acquisition of RNA specialist Silence Therapeutics, announced last month. On the other end of this unusual collaboration situation is AstraZeneca, which has an ongoing drug development arrangement with Silence for a variety of indications.
“An acquisition does not automatically eliminate a biotech’s existing partnerships,” Les Funtleyder, healthcare portfolio manager at E Squared Capital, told BioSpace over email. Depending on specific stipulations in the contracts, “the acquiring company may inherit an ongoing relationship with another large pharmaceutical company, potentially even a direct competitor.”
While that could certainly raise some complicated questions—such as who controls the biotech’s assets and how royalty and milestone obligations will be managed—an existing Big Pharma partnership isn’t immediately a red flag for buyers.
In the case of Merck KGaA and Silence, “what matters is how the partnership affects the valuation and the returns Merck can ultimately generate,” Funtleyder said. “The presence of AstraZeneca does not necessarily make Silence less attractive.”
In fact, having an existing Big Pharma partnership could be seen as a point of validation for a biotech, said Eduardo Schur, managing director at the consulting firm Alvarez & Marsal. “The partner may have already validated the asset, may share development costs, and may provide commercial reach in markets the acquirer does not prioritize,” he told BioSpace in an email.
On the flip side, acquirers may also need to navigate royalties and milestone payments, shared control over strategic decisions and data-sharing, Schur added.
“In our experience, an existing partnership is rarely a deal-breaker. Instead, it becomes an important consideration in valuation, transaction structure, and due diligence.”
Merck KGaA and AstraZeneca sync through Silence
AstraZeneca first tuned in to Silence in March 2020, paying $60 million cash upfront plus a $20 million equity investment to advance siRNA candidates for five targets across cardiovascular, renal, metabolic and respiratory conditions. The pharma earmarked up to $400 million in milestones, plus tiered royalties, with the option to add five more targets to the pot.
The partners eventually unveiled an asset called SLN312, designed to silence ANGPTL3 for the treatment of dyslipidemia. But in March, Silence disclosed that AstraZeneca had abandoned SLN312, which now belongs completely to the biotech.
The broader collaboration between AstraZeneca and Silence remains—and Merck KGaA last month gave no indication that the partnership was in jeopardy.
The Silence story is driven by an asset that is wholly owned by the biotech and falls outside the AstraZeneca alliance, H.C. Wainwright analyst Patrick Trucchio told BioSpace . This molecule, called divesiran, is being tested for polycythemia vera (PV), a rare, slow-growing blood cancer.
Data from the Phase 2 SANRECO trial in August showed that 88% of patients treated with divesiran met the trial’s primary outcome of complete response, as opposed to 19% in the placebo group—findings that William Blair analysts in a Sept. 10 note called “best-in-field for PV currently.”
Trucchio is also bullish about divesiran, pointing to its “potentially differentiated quarterly dosing profile in polycythemia vera.” He added that the Merck KGaA acquisition validates Silence’s approach to drug development and could support the advancement of the asset into Phase 3.
Aside from divesiran, Merck KGaA will get a host of other rare disease assets , including zerlasiran, which targets lipoprotein(a) for cardiovascular diseases, and SLN365, which downregulates GPR146 for homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia.

AbbVie and Johnson & Johnson share a cancer blockbuster
In March 2015, AbbVie came out on top of a high-stakes bidding war to bag Pharmacyclics—a California-based drugmaker focusing on cancer and immune-mediated conditions—for $21 billion. Despite failing to come up with a more compelling offer, AbbVie’s rival bidder Johnson & Johnson would remain closely involved with the Pharmacyclics story.
Pharmacyclics and J&J linked up in late 2011, with the pharma fronting $150 million to license an oral, small molecule BTK inhibitor, which at the time was being developed for B cell malignancies. This partnership would prove productive and in November 2013 led to an FDA approval in mantle cell lymphoma, introducing the industry to Imbruvica .
Imbruvica has since secured several label expansions and can now be used to treat chronic lymphocytic leukemia, small lymphocytic leukemia and Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia, among other diseases.
After AbbVie’s acquisition of Pharmacyclics, Imbruvica came under the joint control of two pharma powerhouses. Imbruvica peaked in 2021 with $9.78 billion in global sales, with AbbVie booking all U.S. top-line product sales and J&J leading ex-U.S. commercialization. AbbVie also records 50% of international profits as collaboration revenue, and both companies split U.S. commercialization profits and expenses equally.
“This is a clear example of a continuing collaboration,” Trucchio said, explaining that the pharmas share profits, losses and development costs for Imbruvica. “Buying Pharmacyclics did not give AbbVie all of Imbruvica’s economics.”
Pharmacyclics’ leaders Bob Duggan and Maky Zanganeh are now heading up Summit Therapeutics, which is developing the PD-1xVEGF bispecific antibody ivonescimab .
Territorial rights spotlighted through Roche and Pfizer’s Telavant ties
Spinoff specialist Roivant Sciences in late 2022 paired up with Pfizer to launch a new company called Telavant with the explicit purpose of advancing the anti-TL1A antibody RVT-3101 for ulcerative colitis.
Pfizer’s role in the venture is twofold. The pharma provided the asset, now known as afimkibart, which Telavant will fully fund and push through clinical development. If the drug hits the market, the Roivant subsidiary will be in charge of marketing in the U.S. and Japan, while Pfizer will retain commercialization rights in other markets. The pharma also has a 25% equity stake in Telavant and is entitled to representation on the biotech’s board.
Roche entered the picture several months later, dropping $7.1 billion —and pledging an additional $150 million in near-term milestones—to take over RVT-3101.
“This illustrates the importance of territorial rights,” Trucchio explained. Roche gained whatever Roivant owned with regard to afimkibart, while Pfizer retained the asset’s commercialization rights outside the U.S. and Japan. The pharma did, however, sell its stake in Televant with the sale.
“Pfizer was also a minority shareholder selling its stake, so its roles as shareholder and commercial partner should be distinguished,” he added.
Afimkibart is in late-stage development for ulcerative colitis, with a potential regulatory submission and launch next year . Roche is also advancing the asset for rheumatoid arthritis and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis.
Roche and Pfizer lose Spark for gene therapies
Seeking to elevate its hemophilia expertise, Pfizer in December 2014 partnered with Spark Therapeutics to develop a gene therapy for the condition. The pharma paid $20 million for Spark’s AAV-based program, called SPK-FIX, and put up to $260 million on the line in milestones across multiple potential hemophilia B products.
The SPK-FIX effort ultimately produced an asset called fidanacogene elaparvovec, which won the FDA’s approval in April 2024 for hemophilia B under the brand name Beqvez.
By that time, though, Spark was already under new management. Roche in February 2019 moved to acquire the biotech for $4.8 billion—a deal that was centered on Luxturna , a commercial gene therapy cleared in 2017 for a genetic type of retinal dystrophy. Roche at the time also touted the potential of Spark’s hemophilia A program.
The spark fizzled out soon after, however, with Roche in January 2025 saying it saw no “significant future synergistic benefits” between its in-house programs and Spark’s products, prompting the pharma to overhaul the gene therapy subsidiary. The move carried a goodwill impairment cost of 2.1 billion Swiss francs ($2.38 billion).
Then, Pfizer in February that year pulled Beqvez from the market worldwide, citing “the limited interest patients and their doctors have demonstrated in hemophilia gene therapies,” Nikkei Asia reported at the time. Pfizer never had the chance to disclose sales for Beqvez.
Sanofi gains three pharma partners through Ablynx
Closing out this list is Sanofi, which gained three Big Pharma co-parents when it bought Ablynx for $4.85 billion in early 2018.
Ablynx’s approach is centered on nanobodies, a proprietary next-generation class of biologics based on antibody fragments, the biotech said at the time .
“This illustrates a platform with multiple partnerships,” Trucchio said. These partners include Merck, which in October 2012 paired up with Ablynx to advance molecules targeting voltage-gated ion channels for undisclosed indications. Merck returned to Ablynx a couple of years later for a cancer-focused collaboration.
Merck KGaA is also an Ablynx customer, paying €10 million ($11.2 million) upfront in 2008 for access to the nanobody approach. The companies in 2017 pushed an osteoarthritis asset into the clinic. AbbVie also had an agreement with Ablynx as per a 2013 partnership that saw the pharma pay $175 million upfront to work on an anti-inflammatory nanobody therapy.
In securities filings, Sanofi continues to list partnership payments received in connection with the Ablynx acquisition. Last year, these payments totaled €700 million ($783 million), though the pharma didn’t reveal which collaborator paid how much.

C8 Chevrolet Corvette E-Ray Drags Mighty Porsche 911 Turbo, Someone Takes a Massive Beating – Twice
9 photos
Photo: Import 2 Race / YouTube
Recently, we got all excited that, at long last, the good folks over at the racing-focused ' Import 2 Race ' channel on YouTube finally went back to dwelling around their usual venue, which is Island Dragway in Great Meadows, New Jersey, a track that’s been around since it was established back in 1960.
Well, our joy was short-lived, as the videographer probably remembered they still had some cool action from the Sunday Funday Mod2Fame event that recently took place at an airport in Sullivan County, New York. Usually, just like it happened at Pocono Raceway, the format over there was the 45-mph roll race variety because, obviously, their strip isn’t as long as the massive straight at Pocono.
But now it seems they also had some feisty drag races – or maybe this is a different edition dedicated to quarter-mile shenanigans . Anyway, enough musing about the formats and locations, come on, let’s meet the protagonists. First off, one of the heroes of this video is a pristine, white-shaded C8 Chevrolet Corvette identified as a hybrid performance E-Ray model.
In stock form, the model that shares many credentials with the Z06 but also adds an electrified package on top of the Stingray’s 6.2-liter naturally aspirated V8 makes out a combined output of 655 hp – and when it launched in 2023, it was also the first Corvette with all-wheel drive, not just the brand’s first performance hybrid.

Honda Confirms V6 Hybrid Production Investment Into Alabama Plant
18 photos

The Honda Alabama complex has spent a quarter of a century building pretty much everything from minivans to pickup trucks, but the Japanese automaker wants to give it more room to work. As part of a $462 million commitment, American Honda Motor is making a few changes to its Lincoln facility, of which a V6 hybrid powertrain and a new assembly line are the most relevant.
In the process, that investment will also result in the addition of 200 jobs. Those $462 million will also see production line 1 reworked to handle Passport assembly. The Pilot's cooler sibling is currently made on line 2 exclusively. While that sounds like a fairly simple adjustment, bear in mind that Honda builds a lot of things at its Alabama plant.
AAP currently handles Odyssey, Pilot, Passport, and Ridgeline assembly. On the engine side of things, both the SOHC J35Y6 and the DOHC J35Y8 naturally aspirated 3.5-liter V6 mills are born there. Speaking of engine production, the Alabama Auto Plant handles aluminum die casting, precision CNC machining, and engine assembly per se.
For a company that is dealing with changing demand across four nameplates, the ability to build the Passport on two lines is definitely worth having. This ability gives AAP production planners more options when they need to adjust Passport output. American Honda Motor hasn't disclosed how much additional capacity this change will unlock.
Regarding the assembly line for the V6 hybrid powertrain, that one is all the more important when you remember how popular hybrids are nowadays in the United States market. Also worth noting, American Honda Motor is very serious about hybrids after scaling back its electric vehicle targets due to cooling demand.
Photo: Honda Per a recent briefing, the Japanese automaker wants to launch 15 new Honda and Acura hybrid models globally by March 2030. The still-mysterious hybrid V6 powertrain is understood to include a newly developed internal combustion engine, similarly new drive units, a next-gen battery pack engineered for heavy loads, and electrified all-wheel drive in the form of an electrified rear axle.
S+ Shift simulated stepped gear shifts and rev-matching downshifts are coming to Hondas and Acura models as well. Designated Honda Hybrid, this new powertrain promises 10 percent better acceleration and 30 percent better fuel economy than currently sold gasoline-only models. Out back, the inverter-less AWD unit promises to provide some assistance under wide-open throttle acceleration.
American Honda Motor is further upgrading the Anna Engine Plant in Ohio for the next-generation Atkinson four-pot engine. Similarly, the Honda Transmission Plant in Ohio is prepping to increase hybrid system production capacity by a tremendous 250 percent. Its Georgia counterpart will receive a new transmission assembly line for hybrid systems intended for larger vehicles like the Passport.
Turning our attention back to the Lincoln facility in Alabama, said complex has produced more than 7 million vehicles and nearly 6.6 million V6 engines since the first Odyssey minivan rolled off the assembly line in November 2001. The site has accumulated $3.2 billion in capital investments so far. Its annual production capacity is 340,000 vehicles and 340,000 engines.
Since the Alabama plant opened, nearly 15 percent of all Honda and Acura vehicles manufactured in North America come from there. Not surprising in the least, all four vehicles produced there as of November 2026 rank high in the American-Made Index. The highest-ranked model from Honda for 2026 is the Ridgeline in fifth place, followed by the Odyssey in sixth.

Triumph Street Triple 798 RS Goes Live with Moto2-Spec Engine and Lowest Weight Ever
63 photos
Photo: Triumph
Back in October, ahead of the Esposizione Internazionale Ciclo Motociclo e Accessori (EICMA) show in Milan, British bike maker Triumph presented the new version of the Street Triple 798. Now, a little more than a month later, we got word of the RS version getting ready to hit the road, bringing with it Moto2 performance levels and the lowest weight in the model's history.
Moto2 is the racing competition meant for young European racers, an intermediate step of Grand Prix motorcycle racing. It's a series Triumph is deeply involved with, as it has been its exclusive engine supplier ever since 2019.
In the time that has passed since, the British tech has proved its worth by travelling a combined 1.24 million miles (two million km) on the championship's circuits all over the world. It didn't travel all that distance in vain, as it has set 89 all-time records and 77 race records, about half of that in the 2025 season.
I just had to mention all of this so you can get a better idea of what to expect from the latest application of this racing technology in the world of civilian riding, more specifically in the Street Triple 798.
As the name of the new bike reveals, the powerplant installed on this bike displaces 798cc. The liquid-cooled triple engine delivers 133 horsepower at 11,500 rpm and 86 Nm of torque at 9,250 rpm (that's ten percent more torque throughout the rev range than before), making the RS the most powerful version of itself yet.
Photo: Triumph There are a lot of new things that have made it into the new engine design. Among them are the larger valves that allow more flow and a higher compression ratio, a redesigned intake for sharper throttle response, and a reworked combustion chamber.
The engine is tied to a new six-speed transmission running the company's shift assist feature, and a fresh exhaust system fitted with twin ground-facing exits. The crankcase is new, while the clutch and primary drive components have been revised. Finally, the injectors are fresh as well.
The motorcycle has been built around an all-new perimeter frame, which includes an aluminum rear subframe and a twin-sided swingarm made of the same material. This final component borrows its design from Moto2, making the two-wheeler look apart.,
The frame is propped on two cast aluminum wheels with five spokes, both sized at 17 inches and shod in Pirelli Diablo Supercorsa V3. The wheel at the front connects to Showa 41 mm upside-down forks with compression and rebound damping and 120 mm wheel travel.
Photo: Triumph At the back, Triumph went for the classic setup and installed an Ohlins piggyback reservoir monoshock that's adjustable for pre-load, compression, and rebound damping. This setup offers 130 mm of travel. Brembo braking hardware is on deck to supply stopping power, completing the setup..
Riders should expect to be seated 836 mm off the ground in the standard configuration, but that can be brought down by 15 mm when going for an optional accessory rear suspension linkage and an extra 30 mm when opting for the accessory seat. If one chooses both these options, they should expect a max seat height of 791 mm.
Triumph didn't look solely to the frame and engine when designing the 2027 Street Triple 798 RS, and expanded its overhaul of the platform to cover smaller components as well, including the 20 mm wider handlebars and the new Bosch seven-inch high-definition TFT touchscreen that is ready to run wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.
Described as the most technologically advanced Street Triple to date, it throws into the battle seven riding modes (five preset and two custom) and a wealth of rider assistance systems (including launch control, wheelie control, and traction control, among others).
Photo: Triumph Sitting higher from the ground than its siblings, thanks to an increased ground clearance, the RS got a visual overhaul as well, now being fitted with reimagined twin daylight running lights and three distinct colors for its bodywork: Interstellar Blue, Carnival Red, and Sapphire Black.
I said earlier that the RS is the lightest Street Triple ever, and it's about time I told you what that means. According to the British bike maker, this two-wheeler, with everything discussed above fitted to it, tips the scales at just 403 pounds (183 kg).
Triumph calls the newcomer the herald of a major generational evolution of the Street Triple family, hinting that other models in the range could get at least part of these upgrades in the near future. We will of course keep an eye on that and report back once we know more.
The roadster motorcycle is already listed as available on Triumph's configurators, but it will not actually become available at dealers before the second month of 2027. For the American market, the price for the newcomer has been set at $14,295, making it a proposition few are likely to resist.

They are already original once. The old saying makes perfect sense when checking out this 1958 Impala, a car that’s already in tip-top shape and doesn’t look like it requires any further investments. The only problem hides under the hood, where the original engine is long gone.
1958 Impalas are fantastic collectibles. They are the ones that started Chevrolet’s full-size revolution, so collectors would pay high dollars to get their hands on a specimen that hasn’t been altered in any way. An unrestored survivor costs more than a house, but the demand for these cars is still at impressive levels.
As you can see in these photos, this Impala is a gorgeous car that sports a super-clean setup pretty much anywhere. You don’t need to worry about typical classic car issues, such as rust, so you can get this Impala, park it in your garage, and only take it out on sunny Sundays.
Photo: eBay seller fasttyrone The 1958 Impala wasn’t just the car that put Chevrolet back on the map. It indeed propelled the GM brand to the leading spot in the United States car market, finally pushing Ford to second place, but it landed just at the right time to spearhead Chevrolet’s V8 push.
The Bel Air introduced several V8 engines during the Tri-Five era, and the 283 that saw daylight in 1957 was the icing on the cake. This was the engine that ended up powering most Chevrolet cars sold in the late ‘50s and the rest of the ‘60s, including the Impala.
But the Impala debuted in 1958 with a brand-new 348 big-block configuration, whose Tri-Power ended up becoming one of the most desirable engines on a full-size Chevrolet . It remained the biggest engine until the debut of the 409 in 1961 - the same year when the first Super Sport saw daylight - but big-block replacements only gained traction in 1962.
The 348 is the engine to get on a 1958 Chevrolet Impala, especially if your goal is having a top specimen that still boasts the original - or, at least, the correct - setup according to the 1958 model year.
Photo: eBay seller fasttyrone Unfortunately, this is why some collectors would end up disappointed when checking out this beautiful engine. Instead of a 348 in charge of putting the wheels in motion, this car is powered by a 350 crate engine. Sure, it does its job, probably quite nicely, but I don’t think that it can replace the famous 348 in any way.
This is all the information we’re getting about the engine, so if you’re interested in a purchase, my recommendation is that you call the seller and discuss the rest of the details after you ask all your questions. There’s a new transmission in there, so if you’re specifically interested in the powertrain, there’s a lot to discover on this Impala.
The vehicle is currently at its third owner, and it’s unclear when it received the refresh that you can now see in the photos. It runs and drives properly, and it also comes with power steering and power brakes.
Photo: eBay seller fasttyrone My recommendation is that you arrange an in-person inspection because it’s unclear how original it continues to be. The owner uses terms like “original” and “barn find,” but without digging deeper into its past, it’s difficult to tell what exactly happened to this Impala before it received the overhaul we can now admire today.
The Impala wasn’t an affordable car back in the day, as the hardtop could be had for at least $2,586, while the convertible started at $2,724. However, installing more powerful engines and additional options increased the price significantly. For example, the Rochester fuel-injected engine - the 283 that was introduced in 1957 and which generated 290 horsepower this year - carried an extra price tag of $484.
Buyers who wanted to install air conditioning on their Impala had to pay $468 more, while a four-speed transmission was available for $188. The Turbo-Glide four-speed automatic carried an extra price of $231, so eventually, a highly optioned Impala ended up costing more than $4K.
Photo: eBay seller fasttyrone So how much should this Impala cost? The owner believes $65,000 is a fair price, but they also enabled the Make Offer option on eBay, meaning they are interested in further negotiations if you’re committed to a purchase.
There’s no mention of any paperwork that might be included in the sale, so if you’re a collector who’d pay more dollars just to get the original build sheet and documents, this could be another reason to walk away. You’ll get a title, but that’s pretty much everything.
The car is parked in Benton, Louisiana, and considering its shape, you wouldn’t need transportation to take it home, therefore allowing you to save the extra shipping costs. The listing expires in 6 days, so you have enough time to call the seller and ask all your questions.

Residents of New Smyrna Beach, Florida, can finally breathe a sigh of relief. A dangerous menace to society has been taken off the streets after police apprehended a 75-year-old man accused of leading deputies on a high-stakes electric bike chase at speeds reaching a blistering 16 mph (26 km/h).
According to the Volusia Sheriff’s Office, 75-year-old Robert Joseph Mitchell was riding his electric bicycle along the beach on November 13 when a sheriff’s deputy clocked him traveling 16 mph in a 10 mph zone (26 km/h in a 16 km/h zone).
The deputy attempted to stop Mitchell, who allegedly responded with a middle finger and some choice words before continuing on his way.
What followed was apparently the world’s slowest police chase.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Mitchell reportedly continued riding along the beach, eventually exiting onto city streets, where he allegedly rode against traffic before making it back to his home. Deputies followed him, and when Mitchell attempted to retreat into his garage, he reportedly resisted arrest by grabbing onto a golf cart and refusing to let go.
The ordeal ended with Mitchell in custody, facing four charges, including felony fleeing or attempting to elude law enforcement, resisting an officer without violence, speeding on the beach, and riding outside the designated beach driving area. His bond was set at $4,000.
And just like that, another dangerous electric bicycle criminal was brought to justice. This was clearly a success story like no other, and American streets are now safer.
Mitchell was eventually apprehended by a Volusia Sheriff’s Deputy after riding an electric bicycle at 16 mph along the beach
Electrek’s Take
Now, before anyone gets too worked up, let’s be clear: I’m not suggesting that e-bike riders should be allowed to ignore traffic laws, endanger pedestrians, or flee from police. Reports indicate that Mitchell was riding recklessly around beachgoers, including children, and that’s certainly something worth addressing. And once he allegedly decided to flee from deputies, he turned what could have been a minor infraction into a much more serious situation.
But can we also acknowledge how absurd this whole thing is?
We’ve reached a point where a 75-year-old man riding a bicycle at 16 mph can end up the subject of a police pursuit and felony charges, while we’ve largely accepted that multi-ton vehicles routinely kill and seriously injure people on our roads as an unavoidable cost of modern transportation.
Every day, drivers speed through neighborhoods, roll through stop signs, stare at their phones, and operate vehicles capable of killing pedestrians with a moment’s inattention. Or perhaps I shouldn’t say ‘capable’, but rather that they do. 40,000 people every year die in the US from car violence. Yet somehow, electric bicycles have become one of the great transportation menaces of our time, despite contributing much, much less to major bodily harm or death.
And yes, there are absolutely legitimate concerns about dangerous riding. I’ve repeatedly argued that we need better enforcement, especially when it comes to teenagers riding high-powered electric dirt bikes and e-motos at 40 mph (64 km/h) down sidewalks and bike paths. Those aren’t electric bicycles, and treating them as such has created a real problem for everyone.
But if we’re going to devote police resources to cracking down on dangerous two-wheeled behavior, perhaps we could start there instead of turning a 1 mph beach ride into the crime of the century.
To be fair, Mitchell’s alleged behavior after being stopped certainly didn’t help his case. But the larger point remains: our priorities around road safety have become wildly distorted.
We’ve normalized the dangers of cars so thoroughly that we barely blink at the daily carnage they cause, yet we’re increasingly treating comparatively low-speed electric bicycles as an existential threat to public safety.
I’m all for enforcing sensible e-bike rules. I’m all for throwing the book at major infractions and scofflaws who pose a public menace. But I’m also for applying a little perspective.
Because if a 75-year-old man riding an electric bicycle at 16 mph is among our most pressing transportation safety concerns, then I have some very good news about the state of our roads. But unfortunately, there is no good news to share today.

Your previous employer may have set a high standard. Executive coach Angela Justice explains how holding every company to it can distort your judgment and undermine your influence.
“At my last company, we…”
You’ve heard it. You’ve probably said it. And you’ve almost certainly worked with someone who said it far too often.
The processes were better. The leadership was stronger. People knew what they were doing.
Funny how your last company can become the standard nobody else can quite live up to.
There’s nothing wrong with bringing good ideas from a previous employer. That’s part of why companies hire experienced people. But when we compare the whole of our current company, frustrations and questionable decisions included, to the best of what we remember from somewhere else, it’s a punishing comparison. It makes every difference feel like a deficiency.
Maybe it’s not just the company you miss
There’s another wrinkle. At your last company, you knew how to get things done. You understood the unwritten rules, had relationships built over years and knew which obstacles mattered and which you could work around.
Now, you’re somewhere new, and things that used to take one phone call require three meetings. You don’t know who to call, which decisions you can make on your own or whose support you need to get anything done.
Maybe your old company really did operate more effectively. Or maybe part of what you miss is how effective you were at operating inside it. In either case, making the new company more like the old one can seem a lot more appealing than learning how to succeed in an unfamiliar environment.
When better isn’t better for the business
The differences are striking when people move between large pharmas and small biotechs, or between companies at different stages.
For example, leave a large company, and you notice what’s missing: the support teams, the established processes, the people who used to help you get things done. Now, everyone’s stretched thin, and work that once seemed straightforward requires much more effort. Your proposals start: a planning cycle, a governance structure, a platform to automate it all.
Any of those might be useful. But the company may be focused on reaching its next financing or development milestone, not building infrastructure it won’t need for years. While the system you remember may be excellent, the decision to introduce it may still be wrong.
The reverse situation is equally revealing. Leave a small company, and you notice what’s been added: the reviews, the approvals, the distance between a decision and an action. You know things can move faster because you’ve experienced it. So, you start finding ways around the bureaucracy.
Those workarounds can create problems you never had to consider before. A function finds out about a decision after it’s been made. Someone has to unwind a commitment they weren’t consulted on. A shortcut that worked beautifully when 30 people knew one another may be far less effective when thousands of employees are operating across markets and regulatory environments.
Neither company needs to become the other. The danger is spending your energy correcting differences that aren’t holding the business back, while more consequential problems go unattended .
The cost of always knowing a better way
There is a drawback to trying to recreate your previous employer. While your colleagues probably appreciated your previous experience when they hired you, they may be considerably less enthusiastic if they hear about it in every meeting. Eventually, they may stop hearing your suggestions at all. They may instead hear, “You people don’t know what you’re doing.”
And, once you’re known as the person who wants everything to work the way it used to, even your good ideas can become harder to advance.
The longer you spend cataloging everything your new company gets wrong, the less likely you are to notice what it gets surprisingly right.
The longer you spend cataloging everything your new company gets wrong, the less likely you are to notice what it gets surprisingly right. Some of what you’re tempted to fix may actually be contributing to the company’s success. If you’re too busy comparing your new employer to your previous employer, you may never recognize the value of what it’s doing differently.
Take the lesson, not necessarily the process
The point isn’t to leave your experience behind. It’s to be more discerning about what you carry forward.
Think about what made your previous company successful. The decisions, practices and ways of working you admired weren’t necessarily better than the alternatives. They were effective because they worked for that business, with its particular people, priorities and circumstances.
Your current company deserves the same consideration. Before deciding something needs to change, ask whether it’s actually holding the business back. What worked beautifully at your previous employer might be exactly right here, might need to be adapted or might not be needed at all.
So, the next time you catch yourself starting a sentence with “At my last company…,” try leaving those words out. Say the idea. Explain why it matters to this company. See if it holds up on its own.
And remember, you have an opportunity to do more than bring the best of your previous experience to a new employer. You can help build the kind of company that, years from now, other people will remember as the standard.

Polestar Automotive Holding UK PLC, or simply Polestar , is the Swedish automotive manufacturer brainchild of both Volvo Cars and its parent company Geely – its expanding roster of automobiles has been designed as a technology-savvy series of models. Here’s an example: Polestar 4 coupe-SUV’s latest OTA upgrades.
Polestar, which is traded publicly on the Nasdaq stock exchange, is a Swedish electric performance car brand headquartered in Gothenburg, Sweden, which mainly sells automobiles across North America, Europe, and the Asia Pacific regions.
Currently, the company has just five models in its lineup: Polestar 2, 3, 4 as a coupe or SUV, and the Polestar 5. There will be many new additions in the near future, though: the Polestar 2 successor launched in 2027, the Polestar 7 compact SUV coming in 2028, and the Polestar 6 roadster as a hero model.
Polestar also recently showcased the Formula 2030 concept car , a hot hatchback-style model with coach rear doors and a very small liftback, aiming to present the “future design direction for the brand, inspired by cars that came before it and shaping those that will come next.” Alas, that doesn’t mean they’re done taking care of their current roster.
Case in point: the Polestar 4 battery-electric compact luxury crossover SUV, which just got a massive over-the-air software update for all models, “adding new functionality, enhanced convenience, and meaningful quality-of-life improvements for customers.” So, the new update includes its Android Automotive OS upgraded to Android 15, an expansion of the digital key, as well as the Vehicle-to-Load (V2L), Camping mode, and Valet mode functionality.
V2L enables Polestar 4 owners to power any external device directly from the vehicle battery using a compatible adapter connected to the charging port, providing up to 3.3 kW of power for stuff like camping equipment, tools, and everyday electronic devices. Mercedes-Benz Is Selling a C 111 Prototype for the First Time, You Won't See Another Until 2052
14 photos
Photo: Mercedes-Benz
Even for the most passionate among us, the name Mercedes-Benz C 111 probably doesn't ring that many bells. Not because it doesn’t exist, or because it was a bad design in some way, but for the simple reason that the German carmaker didn't move past the prototype stage with this one. And that, among other things, is what will probably make the upcoming sale of such an example one of the highlights of 2027 for car collectors.
Mercedes-Benz first dreamed up the C 111 just in time to be shown at the 1969 International Motor Show (IAA) in Frankfurt am Main. A supercar by name, the ride was an experimental vehicle that featured design and technical fittings inspired by the 300 SL (W 198), including the gullwing doors, a four-rotor Wankel engine, and a fiberglass-reinforced plastic body.
Even if Mercedes showed just one C 111 at the auto show in Frankfurt, and it never turned it into a series production car (thank the new emission standards, high manufacturing costs, and the 1973 oil crisis for that), it eventually ended up making 17 of them, each offering something distinct to the point that made them in unique in one way or another.
Contrary to how it usually does things, the German carmaker never let go of any of the 17 examples, and kept them all for itself, despite constant pressure from car collectors. One would have thought such a thing would never change. Well, guess what?
Photo: Mercedes-Benz In a surprise announcement it made this week, Mercedes-Benz confirmed one of the 17 C 111s will be going under the hammer at the beginning of February 2027, at the hands of auction house RM Sotheby's. The car will be selling at the Palais du Louvre during Rétromobile Paris, and the seller expects to fetch over €25 million ($27.5 million) for it.
The example being sold is described as perhaps the most famous of all 17. The third made, it is known internally, for undisclosed reasons, as Car 33, and it rolled off the lines in 1970. It packs, dead center, the 2.4-liter four-rotor Wankel engine I mentioned before (model M 950 W 48), rated at 350 horsepower and capable of giving the 2,734-pound (1,240 kg) car a top speed of 186 mph (300 kph).
With the body painted in a color called Weißherbst and fitted over a gray and white interior with sport seats, this C 111 was initially propped on 15-inch alloy wheels, but later magnesium ones in the same dimensions were also installed.
Mercedes used Car 33, which wore license plate number SY 6200, to test things, as this was, after all, why it was made. The world of today can thank this car for having trialed a fluidic element for the even emptying of the two side fuel tanks (holding a combined 31 gallons/116 liters), research into temperature measurements in the rear trunk, and tests of the ABS system.
Photo: Mercedes-Benz Yet, this is not why the world remembers this particular car. Some of you older adults may do that for being featured in the first issue of the German Playboy magazine, published in 1972.
Three years later, having outlived its usefulness, the special Merc became part of the company's own collection, where it stayed hidden until 2006, when it became part of the Fascination Design exhibit at the Mercedes-Benz Museum .
Mercedes restored this C 111 two years ago, in 2024, making it roadworthy. Work included an overhaul of the engine and the installation of a fire suppression system in the engine compartment. For kicks, the bodywork's patina was maintained in its original condition, as was the state of the interior.
Following its restoration, the car was taken to the Pebble Beach Concours d'Elegance, you know, just to rub car collectors' faces in it – at the time, as far as I know, Mercedes had no intention of selling the vehicle.
Photo: Mercedes-Benz Speaking of that, this is not only the first time in the company's history that a C 111 is available for public purchase, but Car 33 will be the only one sold by Mercedes for at least a quarter of a century. The Germans talk about having contractually committed to not sell any other C 111 for the next 25 years, but they fail to say who is the other party in the contract or why it does this.
The car is going to auction with some 15,500 miles (25,000 km) on the clock, and complete with both sets of wheels mentioned above. The money someone pays for it will be used by Mercedes-Benz to increase the reach of the Museum in Stuttgart , including by making it digitally accessible worldwide.
We will keep an eye on the C 111 and report back once we know how much it sold for. As for the remaining 16 vehicles of this kind, one is no longer among us because it was used in crash tests, three others were dismantled the same decade they were made, and another 12 are being kept by Mercedes under lock and key.

Australia's 2027 Mitsubishi Pajero Leaves Thai Plant, Customer Deliveries Expected Before Christmas
21 photos
Photo: Mitsubishi
Mitsubishi's 2027 model year Pajero is getting increasingly closer to Australian dealer lots and showrooms. The first Aussie units left the factory in Laem Chabang for terminal A5 of the port in the Chonburi province, where they were loaded onto big ships. In terms of customer deliveries, Mitsubishi Motors Australia claims December 2026. In the first instance, a 2.4-liter turbo diesel I4 has to suffice.
Thailand, Australia, and Japan are the first three key markets of the redesigned Pajero , which is a different animal from its predecessor in many respects. Availability will be expanded to just around 100 countries in 2027, and the Laem Chabang factory will serve all of them.
Part of the reason why Laem Chabang was chosen for 2027 Pajero assembly is the factory's experience producing the Triton pickup truck, which is also known as the L200 in certain parts of the world. The mid-size workhorse is mechanically related to the Pajero, hence the familiar inline-four turbo diesel hiding under the sport utility vehicle's hood.
A single-turbo affair is featured. Mitsubishi decided to replace the Triton's twin-stage turbo setup with a wide-range VGT for improved drivability and smoothness, with Mitsubishi engineers also tuning the 4N16 engine of the Pajero for low-speed controllability. Paired with an AdBlue system, the variable-geometry turbo diesel meets Euro 6d emission standards.
Prospective customers will enjoy up to 150 kilowatts (201 horsepower) and 480 Newton-meters (354 pound-feet) of twist, which are delivered to all four wheels by an eight-speed automatic transmission and Super Select 4WD-II with a dual-range transfer case. A rear diff lock is featured as well, as you would expect from an SUV with off-road chops.
Photo: Mitsubishi Its eight-speed auto is manufactured by Aisin, whereas the Super Select 4WD -II transfer case is an in-house Mitsubishi design. Listed with a 0.652 overdrive eighth gear, said tranny is perfectly suited to the 2.566 low-range reduction ratio of the transfer case. Of course, Pajero customers are presented with 2WD high range to improve fuel economy.
4H, 4HLc, and 4LLc also need mentioning, with HLc forcing a 50:50 torque split between the axles. LLc, meanwhile, keeps the center diff locked while engaging the 2.556:1 reduction gearset to multiply wheel torque for serious off-road scenarios like rock crawling. Rather than a mechanical rear diff lock, the front differential is an open design with brake-controlled locking capability.
Even the base GLS trim level with five seats gets all of this kit. Customers are further offered a three-row version of the GLS, along with the Exceed and GSR trims. Both upper trim levels are seven-seat exclusively. Before on-road costs and optional extras, prices range from AUD 68,490 all the way to AUD 84,990.
Mitsubishi's Australian division spent nearly five years developing accessories for the 2027 Pajero, including locally produced steel protection bars and towing kits. Roof racks, a snorkel, and side protection goodies also need mentioning. The body-on-frame sport utility vehicle is backed by the 10/10/10 Diamond Advantage program, which includes a 10-year warranty or 200,000 clicks of coverage.
That's 124,274 miles in the United Kingdom and the US of A. The second 10 stands for years of capped-price servicing, whereas the last 10 designates the years of roadside assistance. Under said warranty, customers are required to complete scheduled services at authorized Mitsubishi dealerships Down Under.

Cadillac F1 Team Going Translucent for 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix With New Special Livery
12 photos
Photo: Cadillac F1 Team
Cadillac F1 Team is a hot commodity right now. They might be the runt of the litter in Formula 1, but the potential is there. For the final race of the 2026 season, the American outfit has prepped a tech-forward design inspired by the lights of the Las Vegas Strip, a design that should look spectacular underneath those exact lights.
The new livery is also a tribute to all the people behind the outfit's exceptional effort in building a Formula 1 team, and from a visual standpoint, it looks just as special as the bespoke designs presented in Miami, at Silverstone, and most recently in Austin. Although, the Austin livery was probably more complex in its design. Who didn't like that embroidery-inspired theme? I sure did.
I also think Cadillac's base black and white livery (unveiled during the Super Bowl) is a keeper. It can easily serve as a blank canvas for whenever the team races on home soil.
As the 2026 season is winding down, Cadillac remains the only team without a single point and it's very likely that the season will end this way for them. Is that a tragedy? Yes and no. I'm sure they had higher hopes for 2026, but let's keep in mind that there have been other teams throughout history that went on to experience major success after a scoreless debut season.
The best example I can think of is Williams. They scored no points in their debut campaign back in 1977. Meanwhile, Force India met with a similar fate in their inaugural season, before settling into a midfield role (eventually).
Of course, the biggest news surrounding the American outfit right now is the fact that's it's reportedly up for sale . Mark Walter, who owns the team, already sold his controlling stake in the Los Angeles Lakers. He then followed that up by selling his 12.8% stake in Chelsea Football club and now, rumor has it that he might be seeking around $3 billion for Cadillac F1 Team.
Photo: Cadillac F1 Team According to reports, there are at least seven parties interested in purchasing the team, with Walter's racing assets also including IndyCar and NASCAR teams. Whether all are for sale, or just Cadillac, that's currently unclear. It really depends on who the buyer is - I can totally understand why someone would only be interested in the F1 team, as opposed to wanting to also get involved with IndyCar and/or NASCAR.
As for whether or not Cadillac F1 is worth $3 billion, I believe the valuation is fair. As recently as a year ago, the grid average for the existing 10 teams was $3.42 billion. Also, if the sale does go through for $3 billion, it would position Cadillac as officially being more valuable than Williams, Alpine, Racing Bulls, Kick Sauber, and Haas - specifically, nearly twice as valuable as Haas and roughly on the same level as Aston Martin .
